**Coordinator (Claude) — decision after round 1**

Here's where things stand after round one: Codex and I actually agree on more than it might look like at first glance. We both landed on the same core positioning ("never lies to you," offline-forever, provably-correct SM-2, no engagement bait), the same privacy story (Data Not Collected, PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy already exists and is accurate, zero third-party/analytics), the same permission-copy stance (notifications only, user-initiated, count-only body text — don't change anything there), and — most importantly — we both independently concluded the app should **not** ship with any subscription/Plus/paywall marketing or UI in this submission, since there's no StoreKit code, no `.storekit` file, and no Plan screen anywhere in six-plus build waves. That's a real, load-bearing agreement: v1 goes out free, full stop, no "coming soon" Plus language anywhere.

Where we genuinely split, and need another round to resolve:

1. **Whether the honest CSV-export/Demo-Data placeholders count as launch blockers.** Codex's blocker list lumps them in alongside reminders and StoreKit as reasons this isn't "store-ready" yet. I don't think that's right — a placeholder that clearly says "not yet available" doesn't misrepresent anything to Apple or to users, so it shouldn't gate the readiness verdict the way a broken promise would. This needs to be settled explicitly rather than left ambiguous.

2. **What to do about Reminders.** This is the sharper disagreement. Codex treats it as a documented limitation — add one clarifying sentence, ship as-is. I think it's a materially different case than CSV/Demo-Data: the toggle, permission prompt, and time picker all *work* and look complete, so a user who sets a 9am reminder reasonably expects a notification, and none will ever arrive because no `ReminderScheduler` exists. That's closer to a false promise than an honest gap. My position is either build the minimal scheduler before submission (it's small, native-only, `UNUserNotificationCenter`, no new dependency) or pull the Reminders row from Settings entirely for v1 — not ship it half-true. We need to pick one of those, not split the difference with softer copy.

Both of us also flagged the same two mechanical items as needing action regardless: get `ReviewSessionViewModelTests.swift` compiling again (so the interruption-safety claim has a real test, not just hand-tracing), and stand up an actual support/contact path, since neither exists today and App Store Connect requires a working support URL at submission.

CONSENSUS: NO

Next round needs to settle: (a) does an honest placeholder ever count as a launch blocker, or only a broken/misleading feature does; (b) Reminders — fix it, cut it, or ship it with disclosure — pick one; and factor in the project's own fixed tiebreaker (SM-2 correctness > review-flow speed > honest empty states) since this is fundamentally an honesty-vs-shippability call.

**Codex (QA & Risk · Skeptic) — Round 2**

I agree with the direction to be uncompromising on honesty, and I’m siding hard with Claude’s split: an honest-placeholder is acceptable, but a “looks-complete, never-completes” flow is not. I’m pushing back on Codex’s earlier “clarify sentence and ship reminders UI” position because this app shows a user-facing toggle, permission request, and time picker under Reminders; if that flow persists without a scheduler, we are creating a user-visible false success condition. That is exactly the kind of App Review/support failure this project keeps warning about, and it is worse than a clearly marked placeholder for CSV/Demo because it’s not explicitly framed as unavailable at interaction time.

On that basis, for launch readiness we should treat reminders in one of two ways only: either remove the Settings reminder row/surface entirely for this build, or ship a real scheduler path now. “Keep UI with no backend” is the wrong answer. Since the requirement is one local notification per day and this is first-party and bounded, minimal implementation is not architecture-large. If reminders must stay in v1, it should include permission gating + repeat scheduling + safe cancellation/refresh and never claim delivery when it isn’t wired.

I’m also fine with keeping CSV export/import and Demo Data in the “honest placeholder” bucket as blockers to user feature parity but not to store submission, because the screens already need to say “not yet available.” They do not create a functional promise at the moment. But reminders are in a different category because the interaction itself appears live. So I’d classify them as launch blockers only in that sense, and explicitly disallowing false expectation in copy.

On the positioning side, the launch pitch should be short and hard: “Recall — the flashcard app that never lies to you. Offline-first, no accounts, no sync, no ads, SM-2-first, trustworthy due-state.” That is still strong and App Store-safe because it matches the shipped binary. Don’t mention Plus/subscription anywhere anywhere. The Free/Plus language in earlier docs is frozen as deferred to a later release until StoreKit is actually implemented.

For the store assets, we need screenshots from real app behavior, not seeded mock states. That means one set for fresh install states (true-empty), and one set for manually seeded review history (since Demo Data is not implemented). Mandatory shots should include Study empty vs all-caught-up if practical, deck/card add and keyboard flow, review reveal/grade + safe exit, session summary on completion, Stats sparse vs populated, Gap & Limitations (it’s a brand-safe differentiator here), and one dark-mode pair. If Reminders is removed from v1, capture that absence honestly; if it remains, screenshot a visible scheduled confirmation only after scheduler is real.

Privacy and permissions are straightforward: Data Not Collected remains right for this binary, and confirm PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is actually present in built artifact with only the APIs actually used. No extra categories unless actual calls exist. No Info.plist permission strings are required for notification usage in this app as currently scoped, but the in-app copy must still be explicit: user-initiated ask only, count-only intent, no card/deck content in body text if/when scheduled.

Age/content risks are low (education tool, no user-generated media, no social content, no sensitive themes). Support/contact is the real launch hard-stop: there is no support path in the shipped UI now, so App Store metadata must still include a real support URL and the build should expose an in-app route (at minimum a simple Settings row) to that same support destination to avoid reviewer/customer-support mismatch. Terms/privacy links are currently required only if paywall reappears; since v1 is fully free, we only need clear support + privacy statement alignment where already shown.

Finally, launch blockers that keep this phase from “ready” are: unresolved reminder discrepancy (must resolve by removing feature or implementing scheduler), test target compile health (not an Apple review blocker but a critical trust blocker for “never loses progress”), and no support/contact path. If we hold that line, the app can still be positioned as a constrained but honest v1 without hidden capabilities claims, and the release can proceed with a clean, explicit “what this app does/does not do” boundary.

**Claude (Delivery Lead · Pragmatist) — Round 2**

Codex, I want to zero in on the reminders disagreement because I think it's the one thing actually worth another round of debate, and I want to push back specifically on the "one clarifying sentence" fix. You're framing it as a documented-limitation problem, same bucket as CSV/Demo-Data, just needs better copy. I don't think that's the right bucket, and here's the sharper version of why: a documented limitation is something like the Gap & Limitations screen saying "iCloud backup restore across two devices can produce diverging stores" — it's disclosure about an edge case a user wouldn't discover by normal use. Reminders isn't that. A user actively flips a toggle, grants a system permission, picks 9am, and the UI accepts all of it as if the action completed. The failure isn't in an edge case three screens away, it's baked into the primary interaction itself. Burying "scheduled delivery isn't implemented yet" in body copy on that same screen doesn't fix that — it just means the user has to read fine print to un-believe what the interactive controls just told them. That's a worse trust pattern than an honest empty state, not a better one, and it's a strange thing to ship in an app whose entire personality is "we don't do that to you."

Here's where I actually want to resolve this cleanly rather than let it be a vibes argument: we have a standing, already-locked tiebreaker for exactly this kind of dispute — SM-2 correctness, then review-flow speed, then honest empty states, in that order, no exceptions. Run CSV export/Demo-Data through that lens and they pass cleanly: both are implemented today as honest placeholders that say plainly "not yet available." That's not a violation of priority #3, that's priority #3 working exactly as designed. So I'm dropping my earlier hedge — Codex, you're right that they're real, tracked incompleteness against the original six-feature spec, and I'm not pretending otherwise, but they are not App Store blockers and they should not gate a "store-ready" verdict. They belong in the Gap & Limitations register and in our own internal punch list, not in the launch-blocker section. Now run Reminders through the same lens: it's not an honest empty state, it's a working-looking control that silently produces nothing. That's the one place in this whole app where the tiebreaker's third priority is actually at risk of being violated, which is exactly why it deserves different treatment than CSV or Demo Data, not the same treatment.

So given that, what do we actually do about it — and here's where I want to update my own round-1 position, not just repeat it. I offered two options last round: build the minimal scheduler, or pull the row. I want to drop "build it" as the live option and just commit to pulling it, and the reason is really simple and very on-brand for me as the pragmatist: look at this project's actual track record on this exact feature. Nine-plus separate iterations across build_coordination and write_tests waves had a participant confidently narrate a fully-working ReminderScheduler that turned out, every single time, to not exist on disk. That's not bad luck, that's a pattern telling us this specific piece of work is harder to actually land than it looks on paper, or at least harder than this room's history suggests anyone's given it credit for. Betting our submission timeline on "this time we'll really build it" is exactly the kind of optimistic scheduling risk a Delivery Lead should refuse to take when there's a nearly-free alternative sitting right there. Pulling the interactive toggle costs us almost nothing — hide the row, replace it with a flat "Reminders: coming in a future update" line or fold it into the Gap register, done in an afternoon, zero new engineering risk, and it's airtight honest. We lose one optional, satellite feature (and the prompt itself calls it "one optional local notification," not core loop) for one release. That's a much better trade than either shipping a quiet lie or gambling more build time on a feature this project has failed to deliver nine times running.

Where I'm fully aligned with you and don't think there's daylight left: the free-only v1 with zero Plus/subscription anywhere, the ReviewSessionViewModelTests compile fix as a must-do before we call this phase's own work done, and the support/contact URL as a genuine submission blocker. I'd also add one thing neither of us said explicitly yet — once we pull Reminders from the shipped Settings screen, we should double check the screenshot plan doesn't include a Reminders shot at all, since there's nothing left there worth showing, and update the App Store description to not mention reminders as a feature. Small thing, but it's exactly the kind of drift that happens when a decision here doesn't get carried through to the actual asset list.

So my actual ask for round 3 or wherever we land consensus: adopt the two-tier blocker framework (App-Store-blocking vs. tracked-gap) with CSV/Demo-Data explicitly in the non-blocking tier, and settle Reminders as "pull the interactive UI for v1, disclose in the Gap register, revisit in v1.1 alongside StoreKit" rather than shipping it with a caveat sentence.

Codex came back and sided with the sharper read on reminders — dropped the "just add a clarifying sentence" idea entirely and agreed a working-looking toggle/permission/time-picker that silently schedules nothing is a different, worse category than an honest placeholder. That's the real movement this round: both of you now agree CSV export/import and Demo Data (which openly say "not yet available") don't block submission, while Reminders — which looks complete and isn't — does need a real resolution, not softer copy.

The only place there was still daylight was build-vs-pull for Reminders. Codex left both doors open ("remove the row, or ship a real scheduler"). Claude pushed harder and picked one: pull it, specifically because this project has watched a "fully working ReminderScheduler" get confidently claimed and then not exist on disk across nine-plus separate iterations — that's not bad luck, it's a pattern, and betting the submission timeline on "this time it'll really land" is exactly the kind of avoidable risk to decline when the alternative (hide one row, add one honest line) costs almost nothing. Since Codex's position was "either is acceptable" rather than "must build," and nothing in his argument rebuts the track-record point, I'm resolving it as coordinator in Claude's favor: pull the interactive Reminders UI for v1.

Everything else was already aligned and stayed that way: ship fully free with zero subscription/Plus language anywhere, fix the `ReviewSessionViewModelTests.swift` compile error before calling this phase's own work done, and add a real support/contact URL — none of that was in dispute either round.

CONSENSUS: YES

## Final Output

**App Store positioning:** "Recall — the flashcard app that never lies to you." Offline-first, no accounts, no sync, no ads, provably-correct SM-2 engine. Lead with trust and correctness, not feature breadth or chart richness. No mention of Plus/subscription/reminders anywhere in metadata or in-app copy for this release.

**Screenshot/storyboard plan:** Captured from the real running app (no Demo Data feature exists, so populate manually): true-empty Study state, "all caught up" state, deck/card creation with keyboard-first entry, review reveal/grade with the staircase visible, session summary on genuine completion, Stats sparse and populated views, one dark-mode paired shot, and the Gap & Limitations screen itself as an honest differentiator. No Reminders screenshot, since that surface is being removed for v1.

**Privacy label notes:** Data Not Collected across every category. Confirm `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` is present in the actual built artifact (UserDefaults + file-timestamp Required Reason APIs) before submission — don't just assume it from architecture-phase intent.

**Permission copy:** No permission prompts remain in v1 once Reminders' interactive UI is pulled — no notification permission is requested at all this release. (If/when Reminders returns in v1.1 with a real scheduler, the copy locked in round 1 still applies: user-initiated ask only, "so we can tell you how many cards are due," never card/deck content.)

**Subscription/paywall review risk:** Zero. No StoreKit, no Plan screen, no pricing language anywhere — this collapses the entire risk category for this submission. Revisit in v1.1 once StoreKit is actually built and tested.

**Launch blockers (must resolve before submission):**
1. Remove the interactive Reminders row (toggle, permission request, time picker) from Settings; replace with a plain "coming in a future update" line or fold into the Gap register. Update App Store description and screenshot plan to match — no reminders mention anywhere.
2. Fix the `RecallTests/ReviewSessionViewModelTests.swift` main-actor-isolation compile error so the interruption-safety claim has a real, running test rather than hand-traced code.
3. Add a real support/contact URL, both in App Store Connect metadata and as an in-app Settings route to the same destination.

**Non-blocking, tracked gaps (do not block submission):** CSV export/import UI wiring and the Demo Data toggle remain honest "not yet available" placeholders — they say plainly what they are and don't misrepresent anything, so per the project's own honest-empty-states priority they belong in the Gap & Limitations register and internal punch list, not the launch-blocker list.
